macro.reasoning: The temperature series shows a clear seasonal peak in late July/early August (31-32.6°C) followed by a sharp drop to 31.0°C on Aug 8 with rising humidity (60%) and light rain, signaling the end of the hot/dry regime. The last 10 days show a downward trend from 32.6°C to 31.0°C. With the seasonal cycle turning toward cooler/wetter conditions and no evidence of another heat spike, a steady decline of ~0.5°C/day is projected over the 7-day horizon, consistent with the observed late-summer transition pattern.

micro.reasoning: Temperature shows a clear cooling trend from the recent peak of 32.6°C on Aug 6 to 31.0°C on Aug 8, accompanied by rising humidity (53% to 60%) and falling wind speed (16.2 to 10.2 m/s). This pattern matches previous cooling episodes (e.g., Jul 20-25, Jul 1-4) where temperatures dropped 4-5°C over 3-5 days as humidity increased and winds decreased. The current trajectory suggests continued gradual cooling toward the seasonal mean of ~28-29°C.

synthesis.reasoning: Both macro and micro forecasts converge on an identical 7-day cooling trajectory, projecting a steady ~0.5°C daily decline from the current 31.0°C. The macro view emphasizes the seasonal transition from the late-summer heat peak (32.6°C on Aug 6) toward cooler/wetter conditions, while the micro view highlights the immediate meteorological drivers: rising humidity (53%→60%), falling wind speeds (16.2→10.2 m/s), and the onset of light rain — a pattern that historically precedes 4-5°C drops over 3-5 days (e.g., Jul 20-25, Jul 1-4). The strong agreement between seasonal and synoptic signals, plus the consistency with multiple historical analogs, gives high confidence in this gradual cooling forecast toward the seasonal mean of ~28-29°C.
